full_judgment:
4. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, was that the suit property measuring .71 acre of land appertaining to three plots of C.S. Khatian Nos. 456 and 458 of mouza Gopar, Police Station-Keranigonj, District-Dhaka belonged to the plaintiff deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha and Hari Priya Baisnabi was the shebait of this deity. That the suit land was correctly recorded in C.S. khatian in the name of deity. Hari Priya Baisnabi used to reside in the suit land and perform the religious rites of the Bigraha. On the death of Hari Priya Baisnabi Khepa Chand Bairagi used to perform the religious rites of the deity at the request of the local persons. That Khapa Chand Bairagi used to reside in the suit land and in S.A. Khatian the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of Khapa Chand Bairagi. That after the death of Khapa Chand Bairagi his two sons tried to dispose of the suit property and as such, on 03.05.1985, local religious minded people formed a committee to run the religious rites of the deity and in 1987 the General Secretary of that committee filed Mutation Case No. 1002/87-88 for recording the suit land in the name of deity by correcting the S.A. khatian and consequently the S.A. khatian was corrected and the suit property was recorded in the name of deity. But the defendant petitioners raised objection and prayed for cancellation of the said mutation claiming title in the suit property and ultimately got the result in their favour. 

 5. The present defendant petitioners contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made by the plaintiffs. Their material case was that the suit property was recorded in the name of deity Sree Sree Gopal Jew Bigraha as a rent receiver and one Hari Priya Biasnabi as its shebait. That Hari Priya Biasnabi used to reside in the suit land and when she grew old and unable to move she brought Khepa Chand Bairagi to reside in the suit property. That in 1948 Hari Priya Biasnabi died and after her death her only heir Khepa Chand Bairagi inherited the suit property and possessed the same. That there was no deity in the suit property and the C.S. recorded bargader also did not possess the same. That after wholesale acquisition the suit property vested in the Government and thereafter in 1951 Khepa Chand Bairagi took pattan of the suit land in his name from government and possessed the same as his own property. That he never performed any religious rites of the deity. That on 31.01.1977 Khepa Chand Bairagi transferred the suit property by a deed of gift in favour of his two sons and wife-the defendants. That these defendants mutated their names vide Mutation Case No. 1052/84-85 and paid rent to the Government. That on 03.01.1990 the defendants came to know that the mutation case had been cancelled and the khatian has been restored. The defendants thereafter filed an objection case which was allowed and the suit land stood recorded in the name of the defendants. That the plaintiffs in collusion with some local notorious persons forcibly dispossessed the defendants from 5x6 yards of land of the suit property and installed a deity there, but in fact there was never any deity in the suit property before. 

 11. We have gone through the judgment sought to be reviewed and also other two judgments of the High Court Division and the trial court and find that all the three courts, on elaborate discussion of all the materials and evidence on record and the facts and circumstances came to the concurrent finding that the suit land belonged to the plaintiff deity and it was rightly recorded in the C.S. khatian in the name of deity and that Khepa Chand Bairagi being a shebait of this deity had no right to transfer the suit property in favour of his sons and wife the defendants.
